evidence.claim: Marietta
evidence.quote: Marietta is a city in Washington County, Ohio, United States, and its county seat. It is located in southeastern Ohio at the confluence of the Muskingum and Ohio Rivers, 11 miles (18 km) northeast of Parkersburg, West Virginia. As of the 2020 census, Marietta has a population of 13,385 people. It is the principal city of the Marietta micropolitan area, which includes all of Washington County, and is the second-largest city in the Parkersburg–Marietta–Vienna combined statistical area.

flags: Omitted the existing ferry’s continuous-operation and only-operating-crossing claims as present service promises: only Wikipedia supports them, with no operator confirmation. Its history gives 1817, whereas material says 1815; cache evidence controls. No ferry ride or crossing is required by this itinerary.

The source for Indiana designation history is a 2005 INDOT PDF whose saved text interleaves columns. Evidence quotes preserve that extraction exactly; readable dates are corroborated for 1996 by the byway organization.
Total lengths vary: archived FHWA 943 miles, 2005 INDOT 967, and material mapped mileage 919.6. Omit the total. Drive follows the material strip west-to-east, from Cairo to East Liverpool.

The Ohio story-map cache contains only a short description, not the claimed Rankin House or detailed Ohio itinerary. Omitted Rankin House for lack of evidence. Material supplies driving order, while cache pages establish the named places.
Cave-in-Rock’s James brothers account remains local lore. Cave geology and Mason history lack underlying primary or scientific sources in the cache; use only the limited cached account.

Fly remains short because independently useful site evidence is limited and current ferry arrangements cannot be verified. The Clark homesite is described as a representation, not the surviving original cabin.
